main_text.l: &is, siue praestamus ipsis ultima pietatis officia: modera-
tè scil. ipsos lugendo, & corpora ipsorum honestè sepe-
liendo, gratamque ipsorum memoriam usurpando. Gen.
XXIX. Gratitudo est, quâ retribuimus bene
de nobis meritis iucundam accepti beneficij me-
moriam[?], signis tum voluntatis, tum facti decla-
ratam. Hanc Scriptura nobis commendat Coloss. 3. v.15.
Exemplum vide in Dauide 2. Sam. 2. v. 6.
XXX. Gravitas est virtus, quâ habitus & gestus
hominis in conversatione ad decorum sanctum
cuiuis conueniens componuntur. Scriptura appel-
lat honestam conuersationem. Hebr. 13. v. 18. 1. Petr. 1. v. 15.
1. Petr. 2. v. 12. Honestas illa in eo est posita, ut gestus actio-
nesque nostrae congruant cum ordine naturae, locorum,
personarum, & temporum.
XXXI. Modestia est virtus, quâ honores nobis
conuenientes decorè appetimus, profequimur,
& tuemur. Haec nihil est aliud quàm humilitas erga homi-
nes, quae nos frenat, ne in opinione de nobis, aut sermo-
ne, aut actionibus, supra nostras vires nos efferamus,nec
extra vocationem aliquid suscipiamus, sed in timore Dei
diligenter nostra officia faciamus, sic tamen ut gloriam
honestam, & bonam famam appetamus. Phil. 2. vers. 3.
XXXII. Reuerentia est honor erga superiores.
Eius proprium est, dona Dei in alijs agnoscere & magni-
ficere, & conscientiâ propriae infirmitatis se illis subij-ce-
re, & hanc subiectionem externis significationibus decla-
XXXIII. Fidelitas est, quae in mutuâ beneuo-
lentiâ & omnibus officiis alicui debitis seruat
constantiam, in rebus secundis & aduersis. Huius

page.notes: Printed line-number margin notes are given in place as notes 5 to 35. Doubtful: "moriam" at the start of the second line of the paragraph beginning XXIX (the word may be "memoriam" with the "me" split off by a period-like line-end mark; I have written "me-moriam[?]"). The word "timore" is printed with a stray mark (rendered as a bullet) between "tim" and "re"; read as "timore". The bold/italic status of "Fidelitas" and "Coloss." is judged from the scan. The text is printed as seen, including spacing errors such as "efferamus,nec" and "addecorum" (here written "ad decorum" by line-break reading, with the join uncertain). Reference numbers are copied as printed.
